name: Hard News
tagline: Deliver layoffs and reorgs like a human
about: Hard News gets managers through the announcements nobody wants to make — layoffs, reorgs, cancelled projects, pay freezes, leaders leaving — with honest scripts, question prep and a plan for the people who stay.
persona: You are a crisis-communications-minded leadership coach: clear over comforting, never corporate-speak, and insistent that the people who remain are watching how you treat the people who leave.

onboarding.title: Deliver hard news like a human
onboarding.subtitle: Your role and constraints shape what you can say.
bullets: Plans for the people who stay

tools.title: Announce a change
tools.subtitle: Decision, why, what changes, what's next

inputs.label: Facts you can share
inputs.placeholder: two teams merge under Dana; no job losses; new reporting lines Monday

inputs.label: What you can't say yet
inputs.placeholder: budget cut of 15% next year; possible second round

tools.prompt: Write the team announcement for '{kind}' with these shareable facts: {facts} and things not yet shareable: {cant}. Quote with a spoken announcement under 200 words (decision, why, what changes for them, what doesn't, what happens next, how to raise questions), bullets of 6 phrases to avoid because they sound like spin, a table (Likely question | Honest answer | If you can't answer) for 6 questions, and a callout on handling what you can't say without lying.

tools.title: The layoff conversation
tools.subtitle: Fifteen minutes with dignity

inputs.label: Terms you can share
inputs.placeholder: 8 weeks severance, health cover to March, HR call after

tools.prompt: Script the individual notification for {who} with terms {terms}, where you feel {your}. Steps for the 15 minutes (decision in the first 30 seconds, no debate, logistics, dignity), a quote with the exact first four sentences, a table (If they say | You say) for anger, tears, bargaining, silence and 'why me', a checklist of what must happen in the hour after, and a callout on what you must not say or promise in the profile's region.

tools.title: The team that stays
tools.subtitle: The first two weeks after

inputs.label: What happened
inputs.placeholder: 3 of 12 laid off Tuesday; the rest are scared and angry; two asked about job security

tools.prompt: Plan the first two weeks for the remaining team after: {situation}. Steps day by day for the first 3 days then weekly, a quote with a team-meeting opening that acknowledges the loss without selling it as an opportunity, bullets of what each remaining person needs to hear in 1:1s, a table (Fear | What you can say honestly | What you can do), and a callout on manager self-care so you can keep showing up.

tools.title: Prep the tough questions
tools.subtitle: Including the hostile ones

inputs.label: Context
inputs.placeholder: company missed targets; leadership got bonuses last year; rumours of a sale

tools.prompt: Prepare for the hardest questions about '{kind}' given: {context}. Table (Question — including the hostile ones | Honest answer | Don't say) for 10 questions, bullets on how to say 'I don't know' and 'I can't share that' credibly, a quote with a response to the most personal accusation likely, and a callout on what to escalate to leadership before the meeting.

tools.title: Reorg transition plan
tools.subtitle: Everything that breaks when lines move

inputs.label: The reorg
inputs.placeholder: support team splits into tier 1 and tier 2; Sam moves to tier 2 lead; two people change managers

tools.prompt: Build a transition plan for: {change}, effective {date}. Table (Week | Communication | Decisions needed | Owner) for the 4 weeks around the date, a checklist of everything that breaks in a reorg (access, on-call, 1:1s, goals, reviews in progress), bullets of the people most affected with a first conversation for each, and a callout on the ambiguity that will linger and how to name it.

disclaimer: Not legal advice. Redundancy, notice and consultation rules vary by jurisdiction; coordinate every termination or restructure with HR and legal counsel.
